A deflating universe in which the dark matter is made of these fermions passes through an epoch of strong, velocity-dependent self-interaction

growth of structure when Newton's constant grows with the deflation (A1, A2). Two effects oppose each other. (i) Gravity was weaker in the past: at a fixed Hubble constant the amplitude today (sigma_8 for a given primordial amplitude) falls, d ln sigma_8/d(gsum/H_0) = -0.317. (ii) The Hubble constant that keeps the angular scale of the sound horizon is lower, the cosmological term takes over later, and matter clusters for longer: with that Hubble constant the net change is d ln sigma_8/d(gsum/H_0) = +0.102, a rise of 0.03 per cent at the rate that lunar laser ranging allows, 0.67 per cent at the rate that nucleosynthesis allows and 1.06 per cent for gsum = 0.1 H_0. The growth rate f = d ln delta/d ln a today rises by the factors 1.0027, 1.0590, 1.0982. The amplitude of clustering is thus almost unchanged while its present rate of growth is not: a deflating universe would show itself in f sigma_8 rather than in sigma_8 (data/growth_deflation.csv)
